title: Naturality and quotient cocycle for exceptional coefficient mates
statement: The naturality conjunct and the successive quotient cocycle conjunct of exceptional coefficient comparison, under the same hypotheses as the parent theorem.

source.place: Naturality and vertical mate-pasting in compatibility (2).

proof.text: Package the actual compactSupportMap components into a private natural transformation by whiskering scalarMate and openIso. Proper finite coefficient extension makes all its components invertible over a Noetherian target, without a domain restriction. Thus comparisonInverse is the component of its inverse natural isomorphism. The defining Hom transpose identifies mateMap with its Mathlib mate. Naturality is therefore naturality of that mate.

Use exceptional_domain_and_counit to place G_r K in the domain of the assumed compact-support cocycle hb. Cancel the invertible first two compact-support comparisons in that cocycle. This gives the inverse-square equation, with both quotientAssociator components and their stated directions.

Apply the proved private generic mate_cocycle_at calculation to the three exceptional adjunctions and the inverse compact-support comparisons. Its proof applies the inverse Hom equivalence, uses the counit formula for each mate, moves the first mate past the second square by naturality, and substitutes the inverse-square equation. Naturality of the Y associator supplies the last counit passage. The result is the stated two-stage quotient cocycle, including both associators.

lean.statement: theorem exceptional_naturality_and_cocycle (l r m d : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hmr : m ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [HasCompactification f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] (hInvertible : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (hb : ExceptionalCoefficients.CompactSupportCocycle l f) : (∀ (K K' : DerivedCategoryModule (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r) Y), DerivedCategory.boundedConstructibleFiniteTor (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r) Y K → DerivedCategory.boundedConstructibleFiniteTor (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r) Y K' → ∀ h : K ⟶ K', (scalarExtension (FiniteReduction.quotient l hmr) X).map ((rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r)) f).map h) ≫ ExceptionalCoefficients.mateMap (FiniteReduction.quotient l hmr) f K' = ExceptionalCoefficients.mateMap (FiniteReduction.quotient l hmr) f K ≫ (rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (FiniteReduction.Coeff l m)) f).map ((scalarExtension (FiniteReduction.quotient l hmr) Y).map h)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (hnm : n ≤ m) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) (K : DerivedCategoryModule (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r) Y), DerivedCategory.boundedConstructibleFiniteTor (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r) Y K → (scalarExtension (FiniteReduction.quotient l hnm) X).map (ExceptionalCoefficients.mateMap (FiniteReduction.quotient l hmr) f K) ≫ ExceptionalCoefficients.mateMap (FiniteReduction.quotient l hnm) f ((scalarExtension (FiniteReduction.quotient l hmr) Y).obj K) ≫ (rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (FiniteReduction.Coeff l n)) f).map ((ExceptionalCoefficients.quotientAssociator Y l hmr hnm).hom.app K) = (ExceptionalCoefficients.quotientAssociator X l hmr hnm).hom.app ((rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (FiniteReduction.Coeff l r)) f).obj K) ≫ ExceptionalCoefficients.mateMap (FiniteReduction.quotient l (hnm.trans hmr)) f K)
